record.paper_title: Recent developments and open problems in the theory of permanents
record.original_question: Let A=(a_ij) be an n x n positive semidefinite matrix, let G be a subgroup of the permutation group S_n, and let chi be a complex character on G. Does the permanent dominate the corresponding immanant, in the sense that per(A) >= sum over sigma in G of chi(sigma) times the product over i=1,...,n of a_{i,sigma(i)}?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $A=(a_{ij})$ be an $n\times n$ complex positive semidefinite Hermitian matrix. Recall that the permanent of $A$ is
$$\operatorname{per}(A)=\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\prod_{i=1}^{n}a_{i,\sigma(i)},$$
where $S_n$ denotes the symmetric group on $\{1,\dots,n\}$. Let $G\leq S_n$ be a subgroup and let $\chi:G\to\mathbb{C}$ be a (complex) character of $G$. Define the generalized matrix function (immanant-type function) associated to $(G,\chi)$ by
$$d^{G}_{\chi}(A)=\sum_{\sigma\in G}\chi(\sigma)\prod_{i=1}^{n}a_{i,\sigma(i)}.$$
Prove or disprove: for every $n$, every positive semidefinite Hermitian $n\times n$ matrix $A$, every subgroup $G\leq S_n$, and every character $\chi$ of $G$,
$$\chi(\mathrm{id})\,\operatorname{per}(A)\;\geq\;d^{G}_{\chi}(A).$$
(Equivalently, with the normalization $\chi(\mathrm{id})=1$ as a linear character or in the form stated above, the permanent dominates the corresponding generalized matrix function.)
artifact.category_tag: Permanents and immanants of positive semidefinite matrices
artifact.status_search_result: The permanental dominance conjecture (often attributed to Lieb, 1966) remains open in general. Recent surveys and papers (e.g., a 2022 arXiv survey by Shchesnovich and a 2024 paper in Advances in Applied Mathematics) describe it as a long-standing unresolved problem, with only partial results known for specific groups, characters, and small dimensions.

status_evidence.title: Lieb's permanental dominance conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Survey describing the conjecture and noting it has remained open since 1966.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is still open in general.

status_evidence.title: Some remarks on permanental dominance conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: 2024 paper providing additional partial results on the still-open conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing partial progress; the conjecture remains unresolved.
